title: Alpha Closes at ₹57.7 Crore Net, Marking YRF Spy Universe's First Box Office Disaster
excerpt: Alia Bhatt and Sharvari's women-led espionage thriller wraps its theatrical run well short of the ₹100 crore club, with a lifetime collection lower than Pathaan's single-day record.
body:
• Alpha's India net lifetime stands at ₹57.7 crore against a reported production budget of ₹100 crore, earning a "disaster" verdict from trade analysts.
  • The worldwide gross closed near ₹95 crore — making it the first YRF Spy Universe film to miss the ₹100 crore global milestone.
  • Week-on-week drops were brutal: ₹46.89 crore in Week 1 crashed to ₹8.54 crore in Week 2, ₹1.94 crore in Week 3, and just ₹0.31 crore in Week 4.
  • The film's entire lifetime earnings fell short of Pathaan's single-day high of ₹70.5 crore on Republic Day 2023.

A Spy Thriller That Ran Out of Ammo

Alia Bhatt and Sharvari's Alpha, the seventh entry in Yash Raj Films' Spy Universe and the franchise's first women-led instalment, has effectively concluded its theatrical run with a domestic net collection of ₹57.7 crore, according to data tracked by Bollywood Hungama. Against a reported production budget of ₹100 crore — with some trade estimates placing the all-in cost closer to ₹150 crore — the numbers spell an unambiguous commercial failure.

The Shiv Rawail directorial, which hit screens on July 3, 2026, across roughly 9,000 screens in India, opened to ₹9.12 crore net on day one and built to a ₹33.48 crore opening weekend. Those numbers suggested a fighting chance. But a 70 percent Monday drop to ₹3.85 crore signalled weak word-of-mouth, and the slide never reversed.

The Numbers in Full

India net collections broke down sharply by week: ₹46.89 crore in Week 1, ₹8.54 crore in Week 2, ₹1.94 crore in Week 3, and a negligible ₹0.31 crore in Week 4. Bollywood Hungama's tracker pegs the final total at ₹57.697 crore net, translating to an India gross of roughly ₹68 crore.

In the overseas market, Alpha opened to $1.65 million (₹15.84 crore) in its first weekend, with the United States contributing $380,510 across 340 screens. Total overseas gross settled around ₹27 crore, pushing the worldwide gross to approximately ₹95 crore — tantalisingly close to, yet firmly short of, the ₹100 crore global milestone that every previous Spy Universe film had cleared.

Where It Went Wrong

Trade analyst Taran Adarsh called it the "weakest film in the YRF Spy Universe," conceding "brilliant action set pieces, stunning visuals, and a few well-executed sequences" but concluding that "the writing simply doesn't connect." That assessment aligned with audience sentiment: the occupancy rate on the second Friday dropped to 12.89 percent, with morning shows filling barely 5.85 percent of seats.

"Weakest film in the YRF Spy Universe... Brilliant action set pieces, stunning visuals, and a few well-executed sequences, but the writing simply doesn't connect. Missed opportunity!"

— Taran Adarsh, film critic

Competition compounded the problem. Dhamaal 4, which arrived on July 10, siphoned screens during Alpha's critical second week, while Hollywood's The Odyssey on July 17 further squeezed its late-run potential.

The film's lifetime earnings fell short of Pathaan's single-day high of ₹70.5 crore, recorded on Republic Day 2023. For a franchise built on blockbuster economics, the comparison is damning: Pathaan collected more in a single Thursday than Alpha managed over its entire run.

What It Means for the Spy Universe

Alpha also stars Bobby Deol, Anil Kapoor, and Hrithik Roshan in a cameo. Produced by Aditya Chopra, it was positioned as a marquee 2026 release for Yash Raj Films. Its underperformance raises serious questions about the Spy Universe's commercial viability, a franchise that once seemed bulletproof after Pathaan (₹1,054 crore worldwide) and the Tiger series.

With 2026's Bollywood grosser chart dominated by Dhurandhar 2 (₹1,850 crore), Border 2 (₹485 crore), and Bhooth Bangla (₹293 crore), Alpha's ₹95 crore worldwide sits outside even the top ten. For context, Mardaani 3 — another YRF release — cleared ₹77 crore worldwide on a fraction of the budget.

Diaspora Reception Was Modest

For the Indian diaspora, which has historically turned up for YRF action tentpoles, Alpha's overseas numbers were a letdown. The $1.65 million opening weekend in North America paled against Pathaan's $6 million debut. Markets like Australia (A$240,366 opening weekend) and Germany (€14,146) reflected niche rather than crossover appeal. The franchise's draw among overseas audiences appears to be narrowing, a concerning signal for a studio that has long relied on the diaspora for premium-priced ticket sales.

What's Next

YRF has not officially commented on Alpha's commercial performance. Whether the studio greenlights a sequel or pivots the Spy Universe in a different direction remains unclear. For Alia Bhatt, the setback is a rare commercial miss in an otherwise strong run. For Sharvari, who co-led her first major franchise release, the film's reception underscores the challenges of launching a new sub-brand within an established cinematic universe.

The market has spoken: spectacle alone no longer guarantees a franchise's floor. Alpha's writing-first failure is a lesson the Spy Universe — and Bollywood at large — cannot afford to ignore.
nri_angle: Alpha's overseas gross of roughly ₹27 crore — anchored by $1.65 million in its North American opening weekend — underscores the YRF Spy Universe's diminishing draw among diaspora audiences compared to franchise hits like Pathaan and Tiger 3.
